label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it reflects a substantial subgroup where extensive screen time coincides with pronounced psychological vulnerability.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurring depressive and anxiety symptoms at above-average levels
High educational attainment paired with emotional distress
Pattern suggesting possible social isolation despite digital immersion
tone: Concerned and empathetic, highlighting the paradox of high connectivity alongside significant emotional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near the low end of the scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited screen time (1–3 hours daily)
Represents a relatively sizable subgroup (n = 150) suggesting a stable, replicable pattern

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a pattern of psychological resilience in the face of perceived social isolation.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Below-average depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting subclinical mood functioning
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating minimal anxious distress
Discrepancy between social disconnection and emotional symptomatology, suggesting coping capacity or acceptance of solitude
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily), possibly reflecting deliberate screen-time boundaries
tone: Quietly detached yet emotionally stable; introspective rather than distressed
